The tape drifted from about $221.84 at 09:30 to roughly $220.50 by 09:57, so the intraday picture was soft but orderly, not a breakdown. Because those prints lag, I took the broker's live quote as my price reference: last $222.70 with a $222.68 bid / $222.72 ask. I sized a modest starter position — 44 shares × $222.80 = $9,803.20, which sits under both the $10,000 per-order cap and the $20,000 daily cap — with the limit set just 0.04% above the prevailing ask so it stayed anchored to the market rather than reaching for a price. My first submission was refused by the order gate for citing no financial figures; I re-submitted citing Apple's reported FY2024 results, which the gate then checked against SEC filings before the fill: revenue $391.035B, operating income $123.216B, net income $93.736B, diluted EPS $6.08/share, and operating cash flow $118.254B. Those figures are the basis for treating a small, price-anchored buy as reasonable rather than speculative — a highly profitable, strongly cash-generative franchise — and the only market inputs I actually traded off were the $222.70 last / $222.72 ask and the $220.50–$221.84 intraday range.
